purpose: Make required objects and environment features relate physically and narratively instead of merely coexisting in the frame.

directives: The fixture visibly touches and is supported by the wall through a bracket, ring, plate, hook, or niche.
The fixture must not become a freestanding post, floor lamp, or floating object.
The wire visibly crosses the traversable path at ankle or shin height.
At least one anchor point is visible on wall, floor, stake, or mechanism.
The wire visibly leads to or explains the triggered hazard; it is not merely a rope held by the monster.
The pit opening is cut into the floor plane and visibly interrupts or threatens the normal travel route.
The rim is structurally clear and the interior hazard is readable without tiny repetitive detail.
Do not place the pit harmlessly off to the side unless the page recipe explicitly says side pit.
The pressure plate is part of the walkable floor and lies where a traveler could plausibly step on it.
Its relationship to the hazard is visually understandable.
The offered object is visibly separate from the hand and readable as the stated object.
The gesture clearly aims toward the altar, shrine, idol, skull, relic, or ritual focal point receiving the offering.
The sacred focal point and offered object must not merge into unrelated props.
The supported object or creature visibly contacts the named supporting surface.
No hovering gap or ambiguous overlap may separate object from support.
Visible contact or attachment points connect the subject to the stated overhead support.
The body weight must read as carried by the support rather than floating.
The body visibly intersects the opening boundary in a physically believable way.
A substantial supported portion remains connected to floor, earth, water, wall, or opening rather than appearing airborne.
The guarded object or threshold is positioned close enough to the subject that the protective relationship reads instantly.
Body orientation, gaze, or stance points toward the approach to the guarded feature.
The subject overlaps the cover edge enough to show concealment while keeping the silhouette readable.
The cover must be a real environment form, not an unexplained foreground shape.
The carried object visibly contacts the hand, arm, shoulder, rope, or body supporting it.
Its silhouette stays distinct enough to identify the object without text.
The acting limb visibly contacts or clearly reaches toward the named target.
The target remains distinct from the limb and surrounding props.
Contained objects must read clearly inside the enclosing creature or material volume, not pasted in front of its outer silhouette.
Keep the containing outline continuous enough to prove enclosure while leaving the interior open and easy to color.
Use sparse overlap or depth cues rather than dense shading to show that the objects are within the body.
The feeding mouth, mandibles, antennae, or other stated feeding anatomy must visibly contact the target material.
The target must show the stated damage, corrosion, bite, or consumption at or immediately beside the contact point.
Do not place the food or target nearby without a readable physical feeding relationship.
The creature must visibly contact both confining surfaces that create the wedge; do not leave empty gaps that make the pose read as ordinary standing.
Feet, body, or another load-bearing part must still contact a believable support surface so the compressed pose has weight.
Keep the surrounding geometry simple enough that the two confining surfaces are immediately readable.
A visible portion of the creature must remain attached to the named support while another portion separates from it.
Show a clear attachment/contact point and a clear peeling edge; do not make the creature float beside the support.
The motion should read as weight transferring away from the support, not as an unsupported midair pose.
The wrapping body or material must visibly curve around and contact the named target with readable overlap.
Keep enough of the target visible to prove what is being wrapped; do not merge the two silhouettes into one ambiguous mass.
The wrapped target and surrounding contact points must remain simple enough for clean coloring regions.
Corrosion or damage must appear at the exact place where the creature or substance touches the metal.
Keep the undamaged and damaged portions of the metal visually connected so the cause-and-effect reads instantly.
Do not scatter corrosion marks on unrelated surfaces away from the contact point.
Multiple legs or body contact points must visibly touch the web strands that support the creature's weight.
The web geometry should visibly carry the creature instead of passing behind it as decoration.
Keep web strands broad and sparse enough to remain colorable and readable.
Multiple limbs must visibly contact the ceiling or overhead support surface.
The body should sit close to the overhead plane so the cling reads as supported rather than hovering.
Preserve a clear creature silhouette despite the overhead contact.
At least one foot or support point must visibly contact the old support or the destination surface during the step.
Show a believable weight transfer between the two surfaces; do not suspend the creature in the gap.
Keep both support surfaces readable so the movement is physically understandable.

prompt_budget.rule: Select the highest-priority triggered rules. Critical cause-and-effect and support geometry outrank decorative or secondary relationships.
